source.title: Insights into the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis and Iterative Magnitude Pruning
source.authors: Tausifa Jan Saleem; Ramanjit Ahuja; Surendra Prasad; B. Lall

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own results on basin volume and test accuracy, and argues that volume alone does not determine generalization. It does not test the versions’ specified claims or measures directly.
record.gate_note: The study reports test-accuracy comparisons for pruning and retraining strategies, plus loss-landscape and basin-volume measurements. Its comparisons do not measure the training-to-test error gap or the magnitude-aware perturbation measure specified in V7. Cited findings are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports pruning, retraining, and basin-geometry results, but none tests V1–V8. Its basin radii and Hessian eigenvalues do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness or its ranking of training-to-test error gaps. The argument against basin volume alone determining generalization therefore does not test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that IMP uncovers well-performing solutions with small volume in the original space, successive IMP solutions have training-loss barriers, and rewound IMP solutions occupy the same connected loss sublevel set. Their geometric account is an empirical interpretation. Any added summary about random pruning leaving that set needs qualification: the ResNet-20 comparator that randomly prunes from level 9 remains in the same set.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines iterative magnitude pruning with weight rewinding and loss-landscape geometry, rather than the claim versions’ interventions and measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Pruning and retraining strategy changes the reported test-accuracy outcome: IMP-WR is reported to outperform one-shot pruning, fine-tuning, random initialization of pruned networks, and random pruning for both tested architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report higher test accuracy for IMP-WR than the compared pruning and retraining strategies on ResNet-20 and VGG-16 trained on CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Iterative magnitude pruning with weight rewinding can outperform the tested alternative pruning and retraining strategies.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report well-generalizing sparse solutions with relatively small basin volume in the original parameter space, with volume comparisons changing after projection into pruned spaces.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Basin volume alone does not determine generalization performance in the studied pruning setting.

record.problems: The reported test-accuracy comparisons are presented in figures without numerical values in the text. The experiments use CIFAR-10 and two architectures; the paper does not directly measure the train-test error gap.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible version-specific result rows. Basin-volume and loss-barrier results do not measure the train-test gap or the versioned magnitude-aware sharpness measure; figures describing these quantities are not treated as evidence for a version.

untested.parts: Natural-label generalization paired with fixed random-label fitting and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test error as network width increases beyond the width required for zero training error; pruning sparsity is not this intervention.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, their association with training-to-test error gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Identifying memorized training examples and comparing their removal with removal of equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text supports the qualitative accuracy comparisons but provides no readable numerical accuracies. The row states indicate that neither comparison can establish a versioned effect; they do not deny the reported pruning advantage. No version-specific omissions require additional rows.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold is not varied.
Convolutional and fully connected architectures are not compared.
Adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers are not compared.
Batch size and training-budget effects are not tested.
The paper measures Hessian eigenvalues and basin radii, not magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, and does not test whether the measure ranks training-to-test gaps.
Memorized examples are not identified or removed.

Section III explicitly reports IMP-WR outperforming the alternatives, but numerical accuracies are unavailable in the supplied figure text. The baseline includes two random-pruning strategies: pruning from level 9 and pruning the dense network in one shot.
